prompt:

and what was measured.

- round 4: Desktop pet shortcut and wake controls guide screen [finish, new_screen]: predicted +7.1%, measured -2.1% (p=0.451069), lost: no clear effect

Previous lessons:
Reordering friction (moving sign-in after pet selection), adding a pet control tutorial screen, and estimated countdown wait info won.
Bypassing onboarding steps (new_flow) yielded mixed results, winning in one test but significantly hurting in another.
Major redesigns and sign-in safety hints significantly hurt performance.
Copy updates, permission checks, layout changes, and notifications showed no clear effect.
Predictions generally overestimated actual gains, but underestimated performance for the tutorial screen and countdown info.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Reordering steps (moving sign-in), estimated countdown wait info, adding a pet control tutorial screen, and personality-driven copy helped performance.
Bypassing onboarding steps yielded mixed results, winning in one test but significantly hurting in another.
Major redesigns and sign-in safety hints significantly hurt performance.
Notifications, layout changes, permission checks, incentives, and most copy updates showed no clear effect.
Predictions generally overestimated actual gains, but underestimated performance for the pet control tutorial screen, countdown wait info, and personality-driven headlines.
